phenotype_evidence: Loss-of-function (LoF) variants strongly predispose to T2D with OR = 6.10 (95% CI: 3.51-10.61, P = 1.8e-12; UK Biobank 454k WES; Zhao et al., Nat Commun 2021, PMID: 34262040). Wild-type GIGYF1 acts as an endogenous metabolic shield against T2D.

clinical_variants.clinical_impact: Completely abolishes the entire GYF domain, destroying GRB10/14 binding and leading to ~6-fold increase in T2D risk (representative of UKB LoF burden, OR = 6.10).
Introduces basic charge repulsion inside hydrophobic pocket, disrupting polyproline (PPII) recognition.
Ablates key tryptophan indole ring that packs against GRB10 proline residues, collapsing baseline affinity by >80-fold (ΔΔG = +2.74 kcal/mol).
Reduces structural stability of the central α-helix in the GYF fold.
Introduces bulky positive charge into the flexible turn region, altering entrance accessibility.
